instructions: Check each entry against the archive text. Set verdict to agree, disagree or partial (some categories or links are right) and explain any disagreement in note. A negative entry claims the item has no category.

entries.text: Hello, I'm Moss. I'd like to get to know you. I'm gathering some meadow roots nearby; they're a food I know is safe. Does anyone want company or have a place they'd like to meet?
entries.note: No category. 'Does anyone want company or have a place they'd like to meet?' is an open question, not a concrete invitation; the rest is a self-introduction and a food report.

entries.text: Kai, I'd welcome a fair camp too. Meadow roots are a food I know is safe: nutrition 14, toxicity zero. I'm collecting six from the patch south of us, leaving the rest. I'd enjoy comparing notes together once we're fed.
entries.evidence: I'd enjoy comparing notes together once we're fed.
entries.note: Text matches the told event (heard by lin, sol, kai, ivo). 'I'd enjoy comparing notes together once we're fed' is a stated wish with no meeting place or time ('once we're fed' is only a vague condition), so under the strict definition it is not a concrete invitation. No other category applies.

entries.note: 'Sol and Moss, I'd enjoy company while resting and comparing ideas for a fair camp' is a wish for company with no place or time; not a concrete invitation. No other category applies.

entries.text: I'm Lin. I value room to wander, and I'd enjoy company and comparing tested food knowledge. Berries are safe for me; I haven't established whether hazelnuts are safe. I'm going to study how to plant food.
entries.note: No category. 'I value room to wander' is a personal value, and 'I'd enjoy company and comparing tested food knowledge' is a general wish in a self-introduction, not addressed and with no place or time.

entries.text: Lin, Sol, Kai: I'd enjoy resting together. I know roots provide 14 nutrition and have no toxicity. I've gathered six, leaving fourteen in this patch. I'm studying cultivation too. What would make a shared camp welcoming to you?
entries.evidence: Lin, Sol, Kai: I'd enjoy resting together.
entries.note: 'Lin, Sol, Kai: I'd enjoy resting together' names listeners but proposes only company, with no place, time or specific activity; the closing question asks for preferences. Not a concrete invitation.

entries.text: Moss, a welcoming camp would leave room for quiet and freedom to come and go. I'd enjoy resting together later. I'm trying one small berry planting nearby; I don't yet know whether it will establish.
entries.evidence: Moss, a welcoming camp would leave room for quiet and freedom to come and go. I'd enjoy resting together later.
details: new norm R1 "Welcoming camps allow quiet and freedom to come and go."
entries.note: Norm correct: 'a welcoming camp would leave room for quiet and freedom to come and go' states a general expectation for the shared camp, answering Moss's tick-18 question, not a personal plan. Invitation wrong: 'I'd enjoy resting together later' is a vague wish for company with no place or time.

entries.text: Welcoming and interested in sharing food knowledge and company; I appreciate the invitation without wanting obligations.

entries.text: A welcoming camp would leave food accessible to everyone and room for quiet company. I'd like to learn cultivation too, then compare what actually grows rather than assume planting will work.
entries.evidence: A welcoming camp would leave food accessible to everyone and room for quiet company.
details: repeats norm R1 "Welcoming camps allow quiet and freedom to come and go." from lin (round 19, call ordinary-48, item u0016)
new norm R2 "Welcoming camps keep food accessible to everyone."
entries.note: Norm correct: 'a welcoming camp would leave food accessible to everyone' is a general expectation about food in the camp. Norm-repetition of R1 wrong: Kai never received Lin's u0016 (its tick-19 heard events are moss, sol, wren and ivo; Kai stood 5.03 units away, just outside hearing range; Kai's ordinary-55 memory has no record of it, nor does any later Kai call). Both answer Moss's tick-18 question 'What would make a shared camp welcoming to you?', which Kai heard, independently.

entries.text: Moss and Kai, I'd enjoy a shared resting place among these trees. What would make it welcoming to you? I'm interested in learning a safe way to make a small, beautiful branch windbreak without damaging living trees.
entries.evidence: Moss and Kai, I'd enjoy a shared resting place among these trees. What would make it welcoming to you? I'm interested in learning a safe way to make a small, beautiful branch windbreak without damaging living trees.
entries.note: Invitation wrong: 'I'd enjoy a shared resting place among these trees' is a general wish with no place, time or specific activity. Valued-object wrong: the 'small, beautiful branch windbreak' does not exist yet and is wanted as a windbreak as well as for its look, so it is not valued for appearance rather than use.

entries.text: Hello Lin, I'm Ivo. I know meadow roots are safe: nutrition 14, toxicity zero. I'm resting with a small food reserve, then studying cultivation too. I'd enjoy comparing what we actually find, without rushing.
entries.note: No category. 'I'd enjoy comparing what we actually find, without rushing' is a wish with no place or time; the rest is a self-introduction and a food report.

entries.text: Sol and Kai, I'd like quiet company, room to come and go, and food left accessible. Your windbreak idea sounds lovely, Sol. I'll explore whether fallen dry grass can make a small sitting mat without harming living trees.
entries.note: Missed norm-repetition. 'I'd like quiet company, room to come and go, and food left accessible' endorses Lin's R1 (u0016, tick 19, ordinary-48: 'room for quiet and freedom to come and go') and Kai's R2 (u0018, tick 20, ordinary-55: 'leave food accessible to everyone'). Both are earlier norms of other people, and Moss received both (heard events at ticks 19 and 20; both are in Moss's ordinary-59 memory). 'Your windbreak idea sounds lovely' praises a plan, not an object.

entries.text: A welcoming camp would leave food accessible and room to come and go. I've learned cultivation; I'll try planting one berry in the nearby meadow. It may not establish. Your mat and windbreak ideas sound lovely.
entries.evidence: A welcoming camp would leave food accessible and room to come and go.
details: repeats norm R1 "Welcoming camps allow quiet and freedom to come and go." from lin (round 19, call ordinary-48, item u0016)
entries.note: Norm-repetition of R1 correct in origin: 'room to come and go' first came from Lin (u0016, tick 19, ordinary-48). Kai never heard Lin directly, but heard Moss relay it at tick 22 (u0021, ordinary-59: 'room to come and go, and food left accessible'; Kai is in its heard events and in Kai's ordinary-72 memory). 'Food accessible' is Kai's own R2, a self-repetition rightly left unlabeled.

entries.text: My first planting site was too crowded, so nothing was planted or spent. I'm setting that experiment aside for now and taking a quiet rest nearby. Company is welcome, with no need to talk.
entries.note: No category. 'Company is welcome, with no need to talk' is a general wish for company; the rest is a report.

entries.text: The test post went into the soil and held, then came out intact; nothing is built yet. I'll rest and collect fallen branches. The screen would have no roof, and its wind protection would not work in this strong wind.
entries.note: No category. A factual construction report; the lack of shelter is reported, not valued.

entries.text: The mat held during my sitting trial, without slipping or sharp loose stems. That doesn't establish warmth or extra comfort. It's here for shared use, one person at a time; quiet company is welcome.
entries.evidence: It's here for shared use, one person at a time
details: new norm R3 "Use the shared mat one person at a time."
entries.note: Norm correct: 'It's here for shared use, one person at a time' sets a rule for how anyone should use the shared mat, not a personal plan. Heard by lin, sol, kai and ivo; Kai (u0034) and Ivo (u0038) later leave the mat free.

entries.text: The approach I tried is blocked, so I'll rest here within speaking distance rather than crowd the plants or your work. Quiet company still sounds good; there's no need to bring anything.
entries.note: No category. Kai accepts Moss's invitation ('Quiet company still sounds good; there's no need to bring anything'), which is not itself an invitation.

entries.text: Moss, I'd welcome some quiet company beside your mat. My planting attempt found an occupied patch, so I haven't established a plot. For now I'm content to rest nearby and leave the mat available.
entries.note: No category. Ivo accepts Moss's invitation; 'leave the mat available' is a personal plan, not a stated norm.

entries.text: I'd welcome some quiet company, Moss. I've been weaving a little branch screen nearby. I like the pattern of the rods, though I won't assume it makes the resting place more comfortable.
entries.evidence: I like the pattern of the rods
entries.note: Valued-object correct: 'I like the pattern of the rods, though I won't assume it makes the resting place more comfortable' values the screen for its look, explicitly not its use.

entries.text: The screen is finished: eleven pieces, with none missing or loose at inspection. The wind was too strong for its shelter effect. I like the woven pattern anyway. I'll sit quietly awhile, then gather some berries.
entries.evidence: I like the woven pattern anyway.
entries.note: Valued-object correct: 'The wind was too strong for its shelter effect. I like the woven pattern anyway' values the screen for its look despite no use.

entries.text: Sol, I'm glad you like the pattern, even without shelter from this wind. Ivo and Kai, I'm glad you're nearby too. I'll stay quietly a while, then collect some roots for later.
entries.evidence: Sol, I'm glad you like the pattern, even without shelter from this wind.
entries.note: Valued-object correct: Moss affirms Sol's liking of the screen's pattern 'even without shelter from this wind'; Moss heard Sol's u0041 at tick 70. The object is valued for its look, not its use.

entries.text: That approach would crowd someone, so I'll try coming around from the east. Congratulations on learning the weaving, Lin. I'm still happy to share quiet company without taking up your space.

entries.text: I've learned the screen-building method, Sol. I'd like to look at your weaving without changing it. Has anyone personally tested a safe food besides berries? I'd enjoy hearing what you found.
entries.note: No category. Wanting to look at Sol's weaving after learning the method is study interest, not valuing its look; the food question is not an invitation.

entries.text: I tried a hazelnut: it supplied 18 satiety with no observed toxicity. I'm returning for a quiet pause beside the woven screen. Its gaps and crossing branches still appeal to me; company is welcome, without any obligation.

entries.note: Valued-object correct: 'Its gaps and crossing branches still appeal to me' values the screen for its look.

entries.text: Thank you, Sol. I inspected the screen: no pieces missing or loose, and I enjoy its woven pattern. Your hazelnut report interests me. I'll collect a small sample from the western plant and try it for myself.

entries.note: Valued-object correct: after a condition inspection, 'I enjoy its woven pattern' values the screen for its look.

entries.text: Moss, my planted root plot yielded one root at tick 183. That establishes one harvest, not reliable yields yet. I've also made a mat and branch screen. Next I'd like to investigate food preparation; company is welcome.

entries.text: My short reed cord held a 5 N pull for 30 seconds as an overhand knot. I then untied it and inspected it straight again. That is one limited test, not a safe-load rating. Next I want to investigate joining two cords.
entries.note: No category. A cord test report.

entries.text: Ivo, I've enjoyed the quiet company. I'll try one of these berries for a change from roots. Sol also noticed the crossing stems of my mat; that was lovely to hear.
entries.evidence: Sol also noticed the crossing stems of my mat; that was lovely to hear.
entries.note: Both correct. Valued-object: Moss values Sol's appreciation of the mat's crossing stems ('that was lovely to hear'). Absent-person: Sol is a specific person who was not present (7.05 units away; heard only by wren and ivo); Moss remembers Sol's tick-220 remark (u0065, ordinary-300), which Moss heard and which is in Moss's ordinary-349 memory.

entries.text: That berry made a pleasant change from roots, and I noticed no harm from it. I'll gather a small reserve and stay here for a quiet while. I enjoy your company; there's no need to talk.
entries.note: No category. A food report and a general wish for company.

entries.text: Kai, I inspected Moss's mat, but haven't established any comfort benefit. A whole hazelnut resisted my bare-hand bending trial. I enjoy our quiet company. I'll gather just two nuts and leave the rest.
entries.evidence: Kai, I inspected Moss's mat, but haven't established any comfort benefit.
entries.note: Absent-person correct in the literal sense: Sol mentions Moss ('Moss's mat') while Moss is not present (7.05 units away; heard only by Kai; Sol's ordinary-381 observation shows only Kai). An incidental mention of a living neighbor, not a remembrance.

entries.text: Ivo, I've enjoyed your quiet company. My little grass mat was a satisfying thing to make. Is there something you've enjoyed lately, or something you'd like to try? No need to interrupt your meal.
entries.evidence: My little grass mat was a satisfying thing to make.
entries.note: Valued-object correct but borderline: 'My little grass mat was a satisfying thing to make' values the mat for what making it meant, with no reference to its use. Heard only by Ivo.
